00e1e33d651bb5ad4c05.baseline:
## Card Element (Deprecated for Link)

> Not recommended — use Link Authentication Element, Express Checkout Element, or Payment Element instead.

Single-line and split (Card Number/Expiry/CVC) forms both supported. Same 90-day auth window. Display requirements: ≥ 350px wide, ≥ 28px tall; popup support required; `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` blocks Link. Disable via Dashboard or `disableLink: true`. Not supported in India.

**Connect**: direct charges + payment methods on connected accounts + full Dashboard → accounts manage own settings; otherwise platform controls.
00e1e33d651bb5ad4c05.replacement:
## Card Element for Existing Link Integrations

The November Web Elements overview still lists Link saving and autofill with Card Element. Stripe’s May and November 2026 dedicated guides no longer recommend Card Element for Web Elements. May names Link Authentication Element, which the May 27 Dahlia changelog renames to Contact Details Element while documenting both Web Elements creation aliases. The November guide recommends Contact Details Element, Express Checkout Element or Payment Element.

Both single-line and split forms use the documented 90-day Link authentication window. Stripe automatically enables Link for granted-access accounts outside India and can selectively show it in production. An enabled sandbox shows Link in eligible sessions. Use test data only in sandbox Link accounts. The typical 350 × 28 px guidance depends on font, locale, placeholder and icon visibility. Pop-ups need opener communication, which `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` blocks. Disable via Dashboard or `disableLink: true`.

**Connect.** Direct charges, payment methods created and charged on the connected account, and full Dashboard access permit connected-account settings control. Cloning methods from the platform, destination charges, separate charges and transfers and lack of full Dashboard access leave control for platform transactions with the platform. Settings for payments without the platform are separate. See [[source-stripe-card-element-link]] and the separate [[source-stripe-payment-request-button-link]] Endive cutoff.
00e1e33d651bb5ad4c05.rationale: Retained the November listing alongside the separate recommendation, followed by the reviewed operational and Connect conditions and exact scope of the Button cutoff.

31206c1f9ee03c16e9f0.baseline: When enabled: if the chosen processor doesn't support a required feature, Stripe auto-falls back. If Stripe also fails, retry processor is not attempted.
31206c1f9ee03c16e9f0.replacement: When onboarding error protection is enabled, Orchestration can try Stripe if the selected main or retry processor lacks a required feature. When Stripe was main and its attempt fails, Orchestration checks whether the selected retry processor can handle the payment and skips it if incompatible. An attempted Stripe fallback can also fail. Without applicable fallback, unsupported-feature request validation can return HTTP 400 `orchestration_unsupported` and name the first unsupported feature. See [[source-stripe-orchestration-feature-support]], [[source-stripe-orchestration-route-payments]] and [[source-stripe-orchestration-retries]].

**Integration.** The November product overview lists Checkout Sessions, Payment Intents, Payment Element and in-app payments. The May acceptance guide covers Checkout, Elements with Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents, Direct API, iOS, Android and React Native. See its dated Mexico-business conditions for Checkout and Direct API. Checkout redirects to `payment_intent.next_action.oxxo_display_details.hosted_voucher_url`. Mobile can show the voucher in an in-app webview. The voucher hub’s separate method-level redirect property has its own scope. The May Legacy Direct API opens a voucher modal with `stripe.confirmOxxoPayment()`. Collected data requires full billing name and email, with each name at least two characters. The helper can use an existing PaymentMethod ID or omit additional data when a PaymentMethod is already attached. The May guide recommends the newer path and says Legacy support could end if deprecated.

The November product overview gives a five-day PaymentIntent default. Both describe a 1–7 day `expires_after_days` option. The response field is `next_action.oxxo_display_details.expires_after`. The November acceptance capture links variants, while their detailed defaults and conditions remain outside that selector. See [[source-stripe-oxxo-accept-payment]].

aadb8d18a10a4efcc967.baseline: Requires beta API version. Creates a `PaymentMethod` object of type `custom`, then calls `paymentRecords.reportPayment(...)` with amount, currency, processor reference, outcome, and timing.
aadb8d18a10a4efcc967.replacement:
The April 2026 Payment Intents Elements, mobile and embedded mobile guides show optional server-side reporting for a payment handled by an external provider. Their examples use `2026-03-25.dahlia` with `invoice_partial_payments_beta=v3`. They create a `custom` PaymentMethod using a Dashboard `cpmt_` type ID, then report the actual processor outcome, timing and external reference with the new `pm_` instance ID. Use `guaranteed` only when the PSP result supports it. See [[source-stripe-payment-element-custom-payment-methods#Recording to Stripe (Optional)]], [[source-stripe-inapp-custom-payment-methods#Optional Server-Side Reporting]] and [[source-stripe-inapp-embedded-custom-payment-methods]].

The November [[raw/stripe-api-payment-record-report-2026-11-07|Report a payment API]] example uses `POST /v1/payment_records/report_payment` with `2026-10-28.endive` and inline `payment_method_details[custom][display_name]`. It supplies no PaymentMethod ID. Its initialized response shows `payment_method: null` and zero guaranteed amount. The separate terminal outcome reporting describes external activity. Payment completion depends on the external PSP’s result. The dated examples leave merchant access and cross-version or embedded SDK compatibility undetermined.
aadb8d18a10a4efcc967.rationale: Merged the three reviewed source routes and kept different versioned request shapes, object IDs, PSP outcomes and optional reporting distinct.
